name: CTimerWorld::CheckForTriggerEventPast
needs: fork body contradicts the exe in ways ours shares: (1) the night window is dead in both bodies — ours tests time >= TIME_NIGHT (99000) && time < TIME_DAWN (27000), an empty range, while the exe's night is the complement of [27000, 99000) straddling midnight: NOT in [31500, 94500) and NOT in [27000, 99000) -> SetNight with m_nLastPercentage = -1 and SetApproachingDawn when time >= 26550, with dawn math confined to [27000, 31500) and dusk math to [94500, 99000); ours instead runs dawn math over all of [0, 31500) and dusk math over [94500, 108000). (2) the dawn intensity carries a spurious negation in both bodies — the exe's dawn branch computes the bare quotient ((time - 27000) << 8) / 4500 with no -1 - (0x54f133: add esi,0xff9688 / shl esi,8 / mul 0xe90452d5 / shr edx,0xc / cmp bl,m_nLastPercentage — no not, no sub from 0xff), while the exe's dusk branch keeps -1 - (0x54f188: or bl,0xff / sub bl,dl) as both bodies have it. Everything else matches: time = m_gameTime % 108000 (TIMESCALE_MSEC_PER_DAY), GetVisibleArea = m_gameAreas[m_visibleArea] (inlined byte index at game+0x37E0, pointer array at +0x37E2), m_bAreaLoaded (+0x1EF), GetInfinity()->m_areaType & 0x40 (+0x624) -> SetNight, day window [31500, 94500) -> SetDay + SetApproachingDusk when >= 94050 (0x16f61 < = TIME_APPROACHING_DUSK), SetApproachingDawn when >= 26550 (0x67b5 < = TIME_APPROACHING_DAWN), /4500 = TIMESCALE_MSEC_PER_HOUR via magic-multiply, SetDawn/SetDusk(n, TRUE), m_nLastPercentage byte at this+5. The fork's only in-function delta is two static_cast<BYTE> wraps around our implicit int-to-BYTE conversions — explicit truncation, no semantic change — so importing fixes nothing the exe contradicts
